column1: #  The audit reported 731 untwinned literals in lib/data as one number. Grouping
#  them by the FIELD they sit in turned that into 27 judgements. Three kinds
#  came out, and only one of them is work:
#    READ     code matches on it. Translating BREAKS it, silently. Listed below.
#    NEITHER  proper nouns - a doctor's name, a book author, a brand, a mother's
#             own post text. Nothing to translate; nothing to record.
#    RENDERED real display copy, and English there is a bug. Handled separately.
#  The Can I? popular chips came out of this same bucket and WERE rendered -
#  `label: 'Pineapple'` beside an entry holding hi: 'अनानास', so the chip and
#  the page it opened disagreed. That is why these are classified rather than
#  assumed: the bucket is genuinely mixed.
#  Search aliases. canISearch() lowercases the query and asks whether any alias
#  contains it. A Hindi alias would never match a Hindi query typed in
#  Devanagari either - the fix for Hindi search is a Hindi ALIAS LIST, added
#  alongside these, not a translation of them.
#  Matched against what a mother types from her scan report, which is printed in
#  English. Translating them makes the lookup fail on the exact input it exists
